[32558 Business Intelligence | Subject description]
Credit points: 6

This postgraduate subject examines the critical role of information systems within business organisations, highlighting how these systems support strategic decision-making and enhance operational efficiencies. You will explore the complete lifecycle of corporate information and knowledge – including its creation, distribution, retention, and application, and learn how to design and develop systems that enhance business intelligence effectively. The subject will equip you with essential skills in system development approaches and knowledge management, preparing you for advanced roles in business analysis and system design. Your learning will be hands-on: through case studies, project-based assignments, and collaborative classes, you will apply theoretical concepts to real-world business problems using various analytical tools. As you work with data sets, you'll enhance your ability to analyse and implement solutions. This approach ensures that you not only understand the theory but also gain proficiency in applying these tools to analyse and solve business challenges effectively.

[32558 Business Intelligence | Learning and teaching activities]
Students learning is facilitated by weekly lectures and tutorials over 12 weeks. There will be one hour of online lectures and two hours of on-campus tutorials every week. The weekly subject content is presented via Canvas. The weekly resources will be made available one week in advance on the subject site. This staggered release format has been specifically designed to promote “distributed practice”. Pre-readings and activities released before classes are focus materials that will underpin actions in each class. Lectures are pre-recorded and provided on Canvas so that the ‘lecture’ can focus on clarifications and Q&As. The lecture material, prescribed readings and online activities will provide students with the information required to engage with the subject content and consolidate their learning. Formative revision quizzes are available every week to provide an opportunity for students to self-evaluate their understanding of subject material.

 Assessment tasks are designed to provide ongoing feedback to students to practice some of the concepts covered in the context of real-life situations. The in-class collaborative activities and weekly case study discussion forums foster student learning to apply theory in practice. Students are strongly encouraged to engage with the case study discussion forums by posting questions or comments and reading, answering and replying to other students’ posts to help build a sense of community and enhance understanding of the content, critical thinking, and written communication skills.

title: Learning outcomes
content:
[32558 Business Intelligence | Learning outcomes]
SLO1: Apply the data to knowledge continuum to describe how business intelligence is used within organisations. (B.1)
SLO2: Apply data-processing techniques and contextualisation for use in accurate and timely decision making. (C.1)
SLO3: Create value for an organisation by using visual storytelling with data. (D.1)
SLO4: Use technical, analytical, and communication skills to demonstrate business intelligence analysis for decision support. (E.1)
